capabilities.principal_scope: enforced by validate_request_auth via _authenticate_registry_write on every mutation route, including this one; the verified actor's tenant is recorded as the entry's immutable owner_tenant (see models.RegistryEntry.owner_tenant) and every subsequent read/write is scoped against it (_authorize_read/_authorize_write)
capabilities.request_identity: generated server-side (reg-{strategy_id}-{version}-{uuid8}); accepts either a name-only draft body ({"name": "..."}, synthesized strategy_id/version 0.0.1) or the full typed body (artifact_type/strategy_id/version) per the 2026-09-06 REGISTRY-STRATEGY-UNIFIED-CONTRACT-001 draft-kind fix — see _resolve_entry_or_draft_payload
capabilities.legal_transition: creates artifact_state=draft or candidate; rejects (409) a second registry_id at an already-registered (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) via a non-atomic best-effort collision guard (see create_next_revision for the atomic version of this check)
capabilities.durable_receipt: RegistryEntry row (registry.entries), no separate command receipt on this route yet
capabilities.exact_version_read: GET /api/registry/entries/{registry_id} (tenant-scoped read; builtins are publicly readable)

capabilities.legal_transition: replaces the entry's metadata record kind only; never fabricates or upgrades artifact_state or a validated StrategySpec; once a reserved key (strategy_spec/strategy_artifact/allocation_policy_artifact/source_seed_id) is set on the entry, this route can no longer change or remove it (409)
capabilities.durable_receipt: registry.command_receipts row when command_key is supplied, keyed by tenant+actor+registry_id+command_key (not a bare command_key) and committed in the same Postgres transaction as the entry mutation; a replay returns the entry snapshot as it was originally committed under that key, never a fresh read of the row's current state
capabilities.status: implemented; immutable-content protection, tenant/actor-scoped receipt keys, and original-committed-value replay semantics added by the 2026-09-06 corrective pass

capabilities.principal_scope: enforced by validate_request_auth via _authenticate_registry_write on every mutation route, including this one; the verified actor is recorded on the RegistryEntry as last_actor
capabilities.legal_transition: a new version for a strategy_id that already has registered StrategySpec entries must be either an idempotent replay of an existing (strategy_id, version) at the *same* registry_id, a legitimate immediate-next semver bump (major+1.0.0, major.minor+1.0, or major.minor.patch+1) from the current latest known version, or declare lineage.parent_registry_ids naming an existing StrategySpec entry for that strategy_id AND be a strictly greater version than that parent's (no downgrade); an arbitrary/out-of-sequence version, a downgrade below a linked parent's version, or a *different* registry_id claiming an already-registered (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) is rejected (400/409). The (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) tuple is enforced as a real atomic unique identity at the store layer (register_if_absent's unique_fields, backed by PostgresJsonOwnerStore.insert_if_absent's table lock / RegistryStore's single process lock) — two different caller-supplied registry_ids racing the same tuple commit exactly one winner.
capabilities.status: implemented; real version/parent-linkage validation added by the 2026-09-06 corrective pass (an arbitrary version like "9.9.9" with no parent link previously returned 200); atomic (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) uniqueness and parent-downgrade rejection added by the follow-up 2026-09-06 REGISTRY-STRATEGY-UNIFIED-CONTRACT-001 rejection-fix pass (two different registry_ids at the same version, and a parent-linked downgrade, both previously returned 200)

bff_adapter_semantics.prior_defect: StrategyCommandAdapter._execute_strategy_action fabricated a resulting_status from a static action->status map and returned an authoritative_readback with zero owner I/O — architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §2. A later fix added real owner I/O but still (a) silently replaced the caller's expected_metadata CAS precondition with a freshly-fetched GET, defeating CAS, and (b) discarded the real PATCH response in favor of a second, independent GET that could return stale/unrelated/empty data and still be reported as success.
bff_adapter_semantics.fix: update_params now requires and forwards the caller's own expected_metadata unchanged (no silent refresh-to-latest), performs a single real HTTP PATCH against the Registry metadata-CAS route, and builds its receipt from that PATCH response's entry snapshot plus its X-Idempotent-Replay header — never a separate re-GET. A PATCH response with no confirmable entry payload raises ActionUnavailableError(AMBIGUOUS_REGISTRY_RESPONSE) instead of manufacturing a false success. submit_review/promote_paper/activate/pause/archive still raise ActionUnavailableError naming the exact owner from command_contract.py.
bff_adapter_semantics.unrelated_scope_preserved: RankingFormula and Ranking action handling in the same adapter file is untouched by this task; their pre-existing fake-receipt pattern is not claimed solved here.

auth_wiring_status.note: architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §3.3 requires reusing services/runtime_auth_inbound.py validate_request_auth with strict mode across Registry mutation routes. The 2026-09-06 corrective pass wires _authenticate_registry_write into every mutating route in service.py (register_entry, register_strategy_spec, register_strategy_artifact, register_allocation_policy_artifact, every advance route, mutate_strategy_artifact_entry, update_deployment_summary) — not just the metadata-CAS route — and additionally rejects a signature-valid JWT missing subject/tenant/role/expiry claims via _require_verified_identity. docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.control.yml already set PANTHEON_REGISTRY_AUTH_MODE=strict and REGISTRY_STORE_BACKEND=postgres for the registry service. This closes the gap the prior generation of this delivery recorded here.
